headline: Philippine Telcos Strengthen Blocking of Sites Promoting Violence
seoTitle: Philippine Telcos Strengthen Online Violence Blocking | FMB News
seoDescription: Converge, Globe and PLDT detailed measures to restrict access to malicious, exploitative and violence-focused online content after renewed school-safety concerns.
deck: Converge, Globe and PLDT detailed existing and expanded controls against malicious, exploitative and violence-focused online content.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Major Philippine internet providers are strengthening measures that restrict access to malicious online content, with Globe Telecom committing to block sites that host gore material and Converge ICT Solutions describing its continuing domain-blocking program.
PLDT had also blocked more than 100 sites streaming videos of school violence following the shooting at Ateneo de Zamboanga University, according to The Philippine STAR.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Converge said it blocked nearly 12 billion attempts to enter dangerous sites and blacklisted around 12,000 malicious domains in 2025. Globe said it blocked 438,446 attempts to access child sexual abuse and exploitation materials during the same year.

The source report does not support the bulletin's claims of a new industry-wide NTC-CICC agreement, participation by DITO Telecommunity, DNS filtering integrated on August 24 or a 15-minute emergency takedown bridge. Those details are excluded.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The measures follow renewed concern about young people's exposure to violent online material after a deadly school shooting. They also raise an important due-process question about how providers identify harmful sites while protecting lawful expression and reporting.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for formal regulatory guidance, transparent blocking criteria and any public reporting by providers on newly restricted domains and appeal procedures.
